Richard Brinsley Sheridan, The School for Scandal, edited by Brander Matthews.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/richard-brinsley-sheridan/the-school-for-scandal

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Richard Brinsley Sheridan, the author, died 1816 (Wikidata Q352725; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Brinsley_Sheridan).
- Brander Matthews, the editor, died 1929 (the facts give no death year; Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brander_Matthews gives 31 March 1929).

First publication of the text used: 1777 (SE colophon: 'The School for Scandal was published in 1777 by Richard Brinsley Sheridan.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1777, before 1931. Works published before 1931 are in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the facts do not name one country of first publication. The possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each of them has a term of life + 70 years or less for these deaths. The last person to die, Brander Matthews, died in 1929, so the text enters the public domain in each of these countries on 1 January 2000. An unknown exact country, or simultaneous publication in two of them, changes nothing.
